THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 24.01.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.192/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, ADDITIONAL MACT, RAMANAGARA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.8,24,700/- WITH INTEREST @ 7% P.A.
FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE DATE OF REALIZATION.
 THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Challenging the award in MVC No.192/2016 passed by the Addl. MACT and Sr.Civil Judge,
Ramanagara, the claimant has preferred MFA No.6465/2019 and the Insurer has preferred MFA No.5840/2019.

sentences.text: 2. For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred according to their ranks before the Tribunal.

3. On 05.04.2016 at 9.30 p.m. when the claimant was proceeding on motor cycle No.KA-42 V 2995 as a pillion rider opposite to RMC Market yard, Ramanagar town, car bearing registration No.KA 05 MB 1017 hit the motor cycle and caused the accident.
In the accident, the claimant suffered grievous injuries.
He was shifted to BGS Global Hospital, Ramanagar.
He was treated in the said hospital between 05.04.2016 to 14.04.2016.
were registered owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle.
The claimant filed MVC No.192/2016 against the respondents alleging that due to the injuries suffered in the accident, he has suffered permanent physical disability and loss of future earnings.
Thus he claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
5. Respondent No.1 did not contest the petition.

Respondent No.2 alone contested the petition denying the occurrence of the accident, rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing KA 05 MB 1017, the injuries suffered by the claimant, his age occupation, income and their liability to pay the compensation.
6.

The Tribunal on recording the evidence hearing the parties, by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No.KA 05 MB 1017 and claimant has suffered 25% permanent physical disability.
Further, the Tribunal assessed his income at Rs.8,000/- per month notionally, applied 18 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.4,32,000/- on the head of loss of future earnings.

The Tribunal awarded Rs.8,24,671/- on different heads as follows:

. awarded in Rs.

1. Future loss of earnings on 4,32,000/-
 account of permanent  disability  2. Nourishment, attendant and 10,000/-
 conveyance charges  3 Pain and Suffering 40,000/-
 4 Loss of amenities & 10,000/-
 enjoyment of life  5 Compensation towards laid 24,000/-
 up period

6 . Medical Expenses 3,08,671/-
 Total 8,24,671/-
7.
Sri S.Raju, learned counsel for the claimant submits that the compensation awarded on all the heads is on the lower side.
He submits that the notional income of the claimant considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

8. Sri B.Pradeep, learned counsel representing Sri H.K.Ramamurthy for the Insurer submits that the claimant himself in his deposition has admitted that he has continued to work and earn Rs.25,000/-
and therefore, there is no loss of future earnings.
He further submits that the claimant himself cogently tendered the evidence before the Court.
That goes to show that there was no loss of intellectual ability as deposed by PW.2 and as held by the Tribunal.
Therefore, he submits that awarding of compensation on the head of loss of future earnings is incorrect.

9. The evidence of PW.2 doctor, Exs.P1 to P6 viz., the certified copies of FIR, complaint, charge sheet, spot mahazar, Crime register and sketch of scene of offence and IMV report show that the Police on receiving the complaint conducted the investigation and charge sheeted the driver of the car bearing No.KA 05-MB-1017.
To rebut the said evidence, the respondents did not lead any evidence.
Respondent No.1 did not even file the statement of objections.
Therefore, the trial Court was justified in holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No.KA-05-MB- 1017 causing injuries to the claimant.

10. The evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and discharge summary Ex.P8 show that the claimant had suffered the following injuries:
i) Fracture of the left parietal bone extending to the temporal bone.

4 ii) Fracture of petrous part of the left temporal bone.
iii) Multiple Hemorrhagic contusions in the frontal and temporal lobes bilaterally.
iv) Left temporo-parietal lobe EDH measuring 6.1 X 1.6 cm.
The aforesaid evidence further show that the claimant was admitted in BGS Global Hospital between 05.04.2016 and 14.04.2016.

sentences.text: He underwent left temporo parietal craniotomy with evacuation of left parietal EDH and underlying SDH under General Anesthesia on 06.04.2016.
As per Ex.P8 his brain was bulging.
Left temporal contusions were noted.
11. PW.2 deposed that such injuries and the procedure has led to 25% intellectual disability.
It is true that PW.1 in his deposition has admitted that he has continued with the same job.
However, he has deposed that due to the accident he is not able to discharge his duties with the same vigour as before the accident.

It is not disputed that he was working as a Welder in GDR Mectek Pvt. Ltd which was the branch of SBM India Pvt. Ltd.
12.
Due to such disability though the claimant did not lose his employment, certainly there is loss of his future career prospects.
Therefore, even if there is no loss of future income, there is loss of future prospects which led to consequential monetary career prospects.
Therefore, the compensation has to be awarded on that head and not on the loss of future income.
13. As per the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 at the time of accident, the claimant was aged 25 years.
For that age and for the kind of his employment he is entitled to future prospects at the rate of 40% of his income.
Admittedly, his income was Rs.13,500/- per month.
40% of the same comes to Rs.5,400/-.
Applicable multiplier for his age is 18.
Therefore, the claimant's future prospects in monetary terms is Rs.11,66,400/-(5400 X 12 X 18).
Having regard to the 25% intellectual disability

,
loss of income on the head of loss of future career prospects comes to Rs.2,91,600/-
(Rs.11,66,400x25/100).
14. Having regard to the nature of injuries and the period of hospitalization and the nature of treatment underwent, the compensation awarded on the head of pain and suffering is on the lower side.
He is entitled to compensation at Rs.1,00,000/- on the said head.
The loss of amenities spoken to by PW.2 is during the period of hospitalization.
The claimant suffered altered sensorium.
Therefore, he is entitled to compensation of Rs.25,000/- on the head of loss of amenities.

The compensation payable on the head of loss of income during the laid up period comes to Rs.
40,500/-(13500 X 3).
On the head of diet, attendant charges and transportation, Rs.10,000/- can be awarded.
A sum of Rs.3,08,671/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of medical expenses is based on the records.
The same needs to be maintained.
16. Therefore, the just compensation payable is as follows:

Hence the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.6465/2019 is dismissed.
ii) MFA No.5840/2019 is partly allowed.
